correctness.rationale: For each odd prime p and h>=1, polynomial factorization on n=r+pt gives p−1 isometries of Z_p. The centered singular polynomial has even symmetry and unit square factor congruent to one mod p, so a convergent p-adic square root provides an exactly bijective coordinate and image alpha+p squares. Counting roots modulo p^(h−1), with p lifts, gives the fiber formula. Period p^(h+1) follows from a congruence and exact n=1 shift witness. The standalone exact checker fully verifies 12 complete modulus-period pairs; infinite validity follows from proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: Primary full texts of Fiorot–Gilblas–Tonolo 2023 and Sun–Zhang 2008 were inspected for periods, surjectivity, branch lifting and targetwise output fibers. Both give strong prior coverage: the period and universality are known and are excluded from novelty. No complete exact fibers of binomial(n,p+1) for every odd prime p and every power p^h were found; the singular square normal form and global p−1+pR count distinguish the new claim. Closest published published-finding corpus results concern k=5 modulo powers of two or p-power lower indices. This is evidence-based originality subject to residual implicit-coverage risk.
residual_risks: The 2008 proof of surjectivity may be extendable to the singular square branch; a stronger implicit or unpublished statement may predate this exact multiplicity formula.
The 2016 global two-index spatial-equidistribution study has only a general abstract comparison, and its results are not a full-text exclusion of targetwise fixed-k fibers.
Indexed published-finding corpus search and published summaries cannot prove uniqueness, and the 2023 paper has broader recurrence machinery that could imply parts of the claim.

value.rationale: The natural question after p-adic universality is how nonuniform the number of solutions to a fixed-binomial congruence is. In the first post-prime column, a uniform family of p−1 regular branches coexists with one singular branch. The theorem fully resolves all odd-prime targetwise fibers at all precisions by an exact quadratic-root formula and locates the only exceptional output congruence class. Its structural singularity calculation is not a routine recomputation of periods or finite sampling.
